title: Copilot Notebooks: add Teams meetings as references
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, administrative paths and automation match the sources checked. It accurately reports the conflicting licensing documentation and distinguishes the existing Notebooks and transcription policies from an undocumented meeting-specific switch.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Current Channel, General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["Current Channel", "General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed in the roadmap record; US Government clouds are not listed.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Android, Desktop, iOS and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap names OneNote and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["OneNote", "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes meeting references as grounding Copilot on discussions and decisions to improve outputs such as presentations and briefs.
claims.quote: enabling users to ground Copilot on the discussions, decisions, and context that drive their work

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can add Teams meetings with transcripts, notes, chats and shared files as Copilot Notebooks references.
claims.quote: Copilot notebooks now include Teams meetings as knowledge sources, allowing users to link meeting transcripts, notes, chats, and shared files within their notebooks.

claims.claim: The release notes say notebooks previously supported only files as references.
claims.quote: Previously, notebooks only supported files as references.

claims.claim: The cited release notes entry is dated August 25, 2026.
claims.quote:
## August 25, 2026
### OneNote
1. **Teams Meetings in Copilot Notebooks** [Android, Windows, iOS, Web]

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented user steps are to open a Copilot notebook, select Add reference and choose a Teams meeting from recent meetings.
claims.quote:
1. Open a Copilot notebook in Microsoft 365.
2. Select 'Add reference' and choose a Teams meeting from your recent meetings.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the underlying copy-versus-link mechanism when a meeting is added.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks meeting references permissions sharing copied linked transcript prerequisites. Opened release-notes and cpcn-permission; they describe linking content, not the underlying copy-versus-link implementation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: How a meeting's permissions apply when it is referenced in a shared notebook is not documented in the Learn material found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "meeting references" "permissions"; Copilot Notebooks meeting references permissions sharing copied linked transcript prerequisites. Opened cpcn-permission and release-notes; no meeting-reference sharing rule found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a separate admin-side default for meeting references.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "meeting" "default"; Copilot Notebooks Teams meetings references admin switch policy Graph meeting references default. Opened cpcn-admin-configuration and release-notes; no meeting-specific default found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Meeting references are user-opt-in: each user chooses a meeting to add.
claims.quote: Select 'Add reference' and choose a Teams meeting from your recent meetings. Searched: Copilot Notebooks Teams meetings references admin switch policy Graph meeting references default; no separate admin enablement found.

claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks are stored in a user-owned SharePoint Embedded container.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages (`.page` files) and Copilot Notebooks are stored in the same user-owned SharePoint Embedded container used by Loop My workspace.

claims.claim: The Notebooks storage container is shared with Loop My workspace.
claims.quote: They do share a single user-owned SharePoint Embedded container with Loop My workspace

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: Notebook storage counts toward the organisation's SharePoint quota.
claims.quote: Storage counts against your organization's SharePoint quota.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks can be shared.
claims.quote: **Copilot Notebooks** can be shared.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The permissions page says notebook recipients gain access to all referenced files.
claims.quote: Anyone you share with gains access to all the files referenced in the notebook.

claims.claim: Access to linked files is granted automatically where possible.
claims.quote: Access to linked files is granted automatically where possible. Some linked files might remain restricted if permissions can't be updated.

claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks do not support external sharing.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks don't support external sharing.

claims.claim: Conditional Access applies to the whole Microsoft Copilot app rather than Notebooks alone.
claims.quote: Only applies at the app level. Because Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are features of the Microsoft Copilot app, Conditional Access applies to the entire app at m365.cloud.microsoft.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Information Barriers are not supported for Notebooks content stored in SharePoint Embedded.
claims.quote: Information Barriers are **not supported** for content stored in SharePoint Embedded containers. Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks use SharePoint Embedded for storage.

claims.claim: Notebooks do not have container sensitivity labels because their container is shared with all Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks don't have container sensitivity labels because they share a container with all Copilot Pages.

claims.claim: No autonomous action is described for adding meeting references.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "meetings" "autonomous". Opened release-notes; the meeting-reference entry instructs the user to select Add reference and choose a meeting, with no autonomous action described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the Notebooks creation policy prevents creation of new notebooks.
claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling creation hides the Notebooks module in the Microsoft Copilot app for affected users.
claims.quote: the Notebooks module is hidden, preventing users from accessing existing Notebooks through the Copilot App.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the policy does not delete existing items.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.claim: The admin policies page says existing items can still be viewed and edited with permission.
claims.quote: Users can still view and edit existing items if they have permission.

claims.claim: Sharing links to Notebooks do not work when creation is disabled through this policy.
claims.quote: Sharing links to Copilot Notebooks don't work when creation is disabled via the policy in this article.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy changes can take up to 90 minutes when policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy changes can take up to 24 hours when no policy configurations previously existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.

claims.claim: Purview eDiscovery supports Copilot Notebooks content.
claims.quote: **Purview eDiscovery**: Supported for search/collection, review (Premium license required), and export as HTML (Premium license required) or original format.

claims.claim: Purview retention policies configured for all SharePoint sites cover Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Retention policies from Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: Audit logs are available for Copilot Notebooks content.
claims.quote: **Audit logs**: Available for all events. Retained, exportable, and streamable to third-party tools.

claims.claim: The compliance summary says there is no admin control to set quota limits on individual containers.
claims.quote: **Limitation**: There's no admin control to set quota limits on individual containers.

claims.claim: A user without a OneDrive site cannot create notebooks if OneDrive creation is disabled for them.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: The Notebooks policy governs notebook creation and use generally, rather than only meeting references.
claims.quote: IT administrators can control creation and use of Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Cloud Policy settings.

claims.claim: The Notebooks Cloud Policy path is Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the Notebooks setting using applyOnce and the documented baseline resource.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
An active `applyOnce` monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The Graph route is preview and supports these Copilot policies only at tenant level.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta. TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: TCM applyOnce fails for the resource if the target setting is configured in any group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and `applyOnce` fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The monitor mode for applying a setting once is applyOnce.
claims.quote: applies a desired-state baseline once in `applyOnce` mode.

claims.claim: The Notebooks baseline resourceType is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks"

claims.claim: The Notebooks baseline resourceVersion is 1.
claims.quote: All resources on this page use `resourceVersion: 1` and are singletons.

claims.claim: Setting properties.value to the string "0" disables the Notebooks policy.
claims.quote: The `value` property is a string, not a Boolean or a number. `0` disables the setting; `1` enables the setting.

claims.claim: Setting properties.value to the string "1" enables the Notebooks policy.
AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in role for applying this resource.
claims.quote: For remediation and `applyOnce`, **AI Administrator** is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: The calling app requires delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for applyOnce.
claims.quote: Creating an `applyOnce` monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated `ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All` permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads

claims.claim: The TCM service principal requires delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for this resource.
claims.quote: | microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks | `CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite` | AI Administrator |

claims.claim: Cloud Policy can scope the Notebooks setting to groups of users.
claims.quote: From the Choose the scope dropdown list, choose either All users or select the group for which you want to apply the policy.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy priority determines which applicable policy configuration takes effect.
claims.quote: If two or more policy configurations are applicable to the same set of users, the one with the higher priority is applied.

claims.claim: The admin policies page documents a two-group Cloud Policy pattern to enable the capability for only a subset of users.
claims.quote: users in **Group A** get the policy **Enabled**, while all other users in **Group B** get it **Disabled**.

claims.claim: The transcription path is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $false disables meeting transcription for the selected policy.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTranscription
Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.
### -Identity
Specify the name of the policy being created.

claims.claim: The existing Teams transcription policy controls whether users can create meeting transcripts.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The Teams transcription policy is not documented as an enforcement point for what Notebooks can reference.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks meeting references AllowTranscription Teams policy PowerShell Graph. Opened meeting-transcription-captions and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; read copilot-teams-transcription excerpts. None establishes a Notebooks reference-selection control.
